question: What is the Delegated Competent Authority section on the URA portal?
answer: Hosted at https://ura.go.ug/en/category/legal-policy/delegated-competent-authority/ and https://ura.go.ug/en/delegated-competent-authorities/ (published August 30, 2023 by Charles Male), this section provides the official designated directory of authorized officials in Uganda empowered to execute international tax treaties, handle Exchange of Information (EOI), and conduct Mutual Agreement Procedures (MAP).

question: What types of international tax exchange are processed by the Delegated Competent Authority?
answer: The Delegated Competent Authority office processes three distinct types of tax information exchange: 1) Exchange on Request (EOIR): Specific, case-by-case requests from treaty partner jurisdictions seeking banking records, beneficial ownership data, or invoice verifications for ongoing audits; 2) Spontaneous Exchange: Unsolicited transmission of information discovered during Ugandan tax audits that is foreseeably relevant to a foreign tax authority; 3) Automatic Exchange of Information (AEOI): Annual bulk electronic transmission of non-resident financial account data under the Common Reporting Standard (CRS) and the AEOI Act 2023 via the OECD Common Transmission System (CTS).

question: How does the Delegated Competent Authority handle Mutual Agreement Procedures (MAP)?
answer: Under Article 25 of Uganda DTAs, where a taxpayer faces double taxation or transfer pricing adjustments not in accordance with a treaty: 1) The taxpayer lodges a formal MAP request with the Competent Authority within the treaty timeline (usually 3 years); 2) The EOI Manager and International Tax Unit review the merits of the case; 3) The Commissioner General initiates bilateral negotiations with the foreign competent authority; 4) Reached mutual agreements are binding decrees and implemented irrespective of domestic statutory time limits.
